clue.text: Cleaned quietly inside vehicle

indicators.note: inside says the quiet letter sits within the vehicle

parts.note: a moped is a small motorised vehicle
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Someone tidied up while sitting silently in their car.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiping a floor with a wet cloth or sponge is a way of having cleaned it.

clue.text: Short boy who asked for more fruit

indicators.note: short means the name is cut off, losing its final letter

parts.note: Oliver Twist, the Dickens orphan, famously asked for more gruel

explanation.surface: A small boy who wanted a second helping of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Twist is the Charles Dickens orphan who asks the workhouse master 'Please, sir, I want some more.'
explanation.definitionFit: The small oval stone fruit of the Mediterranean tree, eaten or pressed for oil.

clue.text: Common pal never dances tango

indicators.note: dances suggests the letters jigging about into a new order

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A friend who never does the tango is a common enough sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widespread or generally found is common, a close synonym.

clue.text: On-line business boss bringing in nothing after October is upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the letters are turned upside down, read from the bottom
bringing in says the boss takes the other letters inside

parts.note: MD is managing director, a company boss

indicators.note: after places the nothing following the month

parts.note: O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A company chief gets nothing out of October and is annoyed about it.
explanation.walkthrough: MD holds OCT plus O to give MOCTOD; 'is upset' turns that upside down in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet company, named for the .com web address, is an on-line business.

clue.text: Glimpsing first bit of gunk beside piercing

indicators.note: first bit of picks out the initial letter of the following word

parts.note: lancing is piercing, as with a lance or a boil

explanation.surface: Spotting a little dirt next to a body piercing.
explanation.definitionFit: A glancing look is a brief one, so glimpsing is its synonym.

clue.text: Let on what poacher handing out freebies did

definitions.meaning: to let on is to reveal a secret

definitions.text: what poacher handing out freebies did
definitions.meaning: a poacher giving away free pheasants or rabbits would literally be donating his illegal game

explanation.surface: Revealing what a generous poacher did.
explanation.walkthrough: Game is wild animals hunted for food, which a poacher takes illegally; the idiom means revealing a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reveal a secret or intention unintentionally, the sense of letting on.

clue.text: Certain hoop inside a bustle getting misshapen

indicators.note: inside places the ring shape within the reshaped letters
misshapen means bent out of form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a hoop is a ring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A Victorian dress with a hooped frame inside a bustle loses its shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting misshapen' rearranges A BUSTLE into ABSLUTE, which takes O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means complete and beyond doubt, so it serves as a synonym for sure or certain.

clue.text: Maybe trainer announced requirement to make profiteroles

indicators.note: announced means the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: a trainer is a sports shoe, an example of the general word

explanation.surface: A trainer, it is said, is needed to make profiteroles.
explanation.walkthrough: The French pastry name is pronounced like 'shoe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Profiteroles are made from choux pastry, a light dough baked into hollow puffs.

clue.text: Near rush to imbibe whiskey, that's habit of one retiring

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to tear is to rush along
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A drinker hurries to down a whiskey before bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A habit is a garment, as in a monk's habit; one retiring is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nighties are the clothing worn by someone going to bed for the night.

clue.text: Appreciate eastern Cornwall town's biscuits

parts.note: to dig something is slang for appreciating it
St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall, the 's belonging to its name

explanation.surface: Enjoy the biscuits of a Cornish seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall, the county at England's south-west tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain semi-sweet wholemeal biscuits, popular in Britain with tea, carry this name.

clue.text: Indulgence consumed by major gymnast

indicators.note: consumed by says the letters are swallowed within the following words

explanation.surface: A senior gymnast gives in to a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a bout of excessive indulgence in some pleasure.

clue.text: Consider overwhelming Spain in marine attack

indicators.note: overwhelming means engulfing, so the sea surrounds the letter for Spain

parts.note: marine means of the sea
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
a bout is an attack, as of illness

explanation.surface: Think about a naval assault that swamps Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To see about something is to attend to it or think it over, so consider is a synonym.

clue.text: Sloppiness from the French kiss, one totally discontented

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
X is the cross that stands for a kiss
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: discontented means emptied of contents, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A French kiss leaves someone thoroughly unhappy with its sloppiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Laxity is slackness or carelessness, the quality of being lax.

clue.text: Trim left side of boundary to make another

indicators.note: trim the left side means cut off the first letter

parts.note: a hedge is a boundary between fields or gardens

explanation.surface: A gardener trims one side of a hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' looks like the definition but is the deletion; 'another' refers back to the boundary, giving another word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a border or limit, so it is a second kind of boundary.

clue.text: Heading off fraud suspect with entry ticket

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order
heading off removes the head, the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone stops a con man who has an entry ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' drops F from fraud, and RAUD with ENTRY is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A British rail ticket valid for travel there and back on the same day.

clue.text: Long time wound up with former lover to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with puts the former partner at the front

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ended means finished, wound up

explanation.surface: A lengthy relationship finished, starting with an ex.
explanation.definitionFit: Extended means lengthened or prolonged, so it is a synonym for long.

clue.text: Climbing in automobile, silver and gold, to go up country

indicators.note: in a down light, climbing means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a car is an automobile
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: to go up in a down light means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Driving up a country road in a car laden with silver and gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' turns IN to NI and 'to go up' turns AU to UA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicaragua is a nation in Central America, an example of a country.

clue.text: Clandestine groups entering unknown into vaults

indicators.note: entering says one piece goes in the other
into names the piece that is entered

parts.note: vaults as a verb means springs or leaps
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Secret cells break into bank vaults.
explanation.definitionFit: Spy rings are networks of secret agents working covertly together.

clue.text: Work in a sty, I'd fancy there's no worse place

indicators.note: in places the piece of work within the other letters
fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Labouring in a pigsty, someone thinks it the worst place on earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges A STY I'D to DYSTIA, which takes OP inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A dystopia is an imagined society of the worst possible kind, the opposite of utopia.

clue.text: Unceremonious over leaving playing area

indicators.note: leaving says the over letter departs from the area

parts.note: a court is a playing area, as for tennis
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: An abrupt departure from the court or pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, abbreviated O.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt means brusque and short in manner, without courtesy or ceremony.

clue.text: Moving down river, overseas on boat, perhaps

indicators.note: moving down in a down light shifts the letter lower in the word

parts.note: abroad means overseas

explanation.surface: Sailing downriver and overseas on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a ship, train or plane is being on board; a boat is one example.

clue.text: Swordsman runs after handler of stolen goods

indicators.note: after puts the runs letter behind the dealer

parts.note: a fence is a receiver of stolen property
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A sword fighter flees after the receiver of the loot.
explanation.definitionFit: One who practises fencing with foil, epee or sabre is a swordsman.

clue.text: Stroke in slow movement

definitions.meaning: the front ... is a swimming stroke
to move at a snail's pace, as traffic does

explanation.surface: A swimmer's stroke done in slow motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a freestyle swimming stroke and a very slow pace of progress, as in traffic.

clue.text: Got on space vessel within berth

parts.note: an em is a printer's space

indicators.note: within puts the vessel inside the berth

parts.note: a berth is a bed, as on a ship
an ark is a vessel, like Noah's

explanation.surface: A boat in its berth was boarded.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go aboard a ship, so the past tense means got on.

clue.text: Something happening in square that's close

parts.note: a close contest is an even one
a T-square is a drawing tool, giving T

explanation.surface: Something going on in a town square that is nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence, anything that takes place.

clue.text: Sea creature is a food with shell on back

indicators.note: on back means read backwards

parts.note: a nut is a food that comes in a shell

explanation.surface: A sea creature that is edible and carries a shell on its back, like a turtle.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuna is a large ocean fish, an example of a sea creature.

clue.text: Modern mobile few in England ordered

indicators.note: in places the first reworked piece inside the second
ordered says the country's letters are put into a new order
mobile means movable, so the three letters of few shift about

explanation.surface: Few people in England bought the new mobile phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Newfangled describes something new and unfamiliar, often disapprovingly, so modern fits.

clue.text: Trashy clubs girl in Putney regularly ignored

indicators.note: in places the clubs and girl inside the other letters
regularly ignored means every other letter is dropped, keeping the rest

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Tacky nightclubs, and a girl in Putney is snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: Putney is a district of south-west London; alternate letters give UNY, which holds C and LASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking class or style, so cheap and vulgar, which is trashy.

clue.text: Want expensive threads, leaving studies aside

parts.note: dear means expensive

indicators.note: leaving says the studies letters are taken away
aside reinforces that those letters are put to one side

parts.note: reads as a verb means studies

explanation.surface: Wanting costly clothes, someone abandons their studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' looks like a verb but means lack; 'leaving ... aside' removes READS from THREADS, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a lack or scarcity, the noun sense of want.
